text: Sara Ullrika Watkins (born June 8, 1981) is an American singer-songwriter and fiddler who debuted in 1989 as the fiddler in Nickel Creek, the progressive bluegrass group she formed with her brother Sean and mandolinist Chris Thile. In addition to singing and fiddling, she plays the ukulele, guitar, and percussion, having performed percussion while touring with The Decemberists. In 2012, she and her brother toured with Jackson Browne during his "I'll Do Anything" acoustic winter tour. With Nickel Creek, she released five studio albums, one compilation, and seven singles. During the band's seven-year hiatus, she released three solo albums: Sara Watkins and Sun Midnight Sun on Nonesuch Records and Young in All the Wrong Ways on New West Records. In late 2005, she stated in a PopMatters interview that writing songs is a challenge for her and her brother, noting it doesn't come easily despite the brothers' long experience. She signed as a solo artist with Nonesuch Records in fall 2008 and released her self-titled debut solo album on April 7, 2009, which she began recording in February 2008 and jointly recorded in Nashville and Los Angeles. The album was produced by John Paul Jones of Led Zeppelin fame, with whom she first performed on a Mutual Admiration Society tour in 2004. In 2008, she toured the United States as an opening act, performing with Tift Merritt on the West Coast in March and April and with Robert Earl Keen in New England in September, as well as a 17-date tour with Donavon Frankenreiter in October. On April 14, 2009, she appeared on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon with John Paul Jones on bass, Questlove of The Roots on drums, and her brother Sean on guitar. On August 28, 2011, she made her debut with A Prairie Home Companion at the Minnesota State Fair. In September 2011, she announced via Twitter she would begin work on a second album in the fall of 2011. In May 2012, she released her second solo album, Sun Midnight Sun, on Nonesuch Records, produced by Blake Mills, featuring guest appearances from Fiona Apple and Jackson Browne. In 2016, she won "Instrumentalist of the Year" at the Americana Music Honors & Awards. In 2002, she starred in a Cingular Wireless advertisement with her former fiddle teacher Dennis Caplinger and other bluegrass artists. Between 2000 and 2004, she collaborated with Chris Thile, Sean Watkins, Glen Phillips, John Paul Jones, and Pete Thomas on the EP Mutual Admiration Society Solo Sampler, the album Mutual Admiration Society (recorded in 2000), and a brief tour. The 2007 documentary Arctic Tale included a song by Watkins and Grant-Lee Phillips titled "Song of the North (Beneath the Sun)," with her vocals alongside Aimee Mann and Brian Wilson. In January 2008, Billboard reported a new supergroup named The Scrolls, later renamed Works Progress Administration (W.P.A.), composed of Watkins, her brother Sean (guitar), Glen Phillips (guitar, vocals), Benmont Tench (piano), Luke Bulla (fiddle), Greg Leisz (various), Pete Thomas (drums), and Davey Faragher (bass), which released their album WPA in September 2009. She is featured on Needtobreathe's 2009 CD The Outsiders on the track "Stones Under Rushing Water." In late January and early February 2010, she toured with Jerry Douglas and Aly Bain in Scotland and England under the "Transatlantic Sessions" banner, culminating in a performance at the Royal Festival Hall in London on February 6, 2010. In June 2010, she appeared on the Nerdist podcast performing "Long Hot Summer Days," a John Hartford cover. Later that summer, she participated in the Summer Love Tour with Garrison Keillor across the United States and guest hosted his show, A Prairie Home Companion, on January 15, 2011. She contributed fiddle, guitar, percussion, and vocals on The Decemberists' 2011 tour. In 2011, she and her brother began performing in the humor/retro-radio podcast "Thrilling Adventure Hour." She played violin and sang on "A Face To Call Home" on John Mayer's 2012 album Born and Raised. From 2012 to 2013, she toured with Jackson Browne as an opening act and accompanied him during performances. Watkins and her brother regularly perform at the Largo nightclub in Los Angeles as "Watkins Family Hour," with keyboardist Benmont Tench and bassist Sebastian Steinberg as regular participants, and other guest musicians such as Jon Brion, Fiona Apple, Don Heffington, Greg Leisz, and Chris Thile when in town. These collaborations led to a 2015 album and tour under the same name. In 2015, she toured extensively with Sarah Jarosz and Aoife O'Donovan (of Crooked Still fame), who later formed the group I'm With Her, and the trio hosted A Prairie Home Companion on October 10, 2015. She also performed vocals for "June & Johnny" on Jon Foreman's 2015 EP The Wonderlands: Darkness. In 2020, she played fiddle on Phoebe Bridgers's record Punisher, on track 10 "Graceland Too." In 2021, she played fiddle on The Killers's record Pressure Machine (tracks: West Fields, Cody, Pressure Machine) and violin on In Another Life. On August 16, 2008, she married Todd Cooper in her parents' backyard in Vista, California. On June 15, 2017, she announced via Twitter that she and her husband were expecting a child in September.
